`advance-400.ttf` is an original synthetic font generated by
`scripts/generate-browser-font-fixtures.py`, copied here so the view crate's
standalone tests do not depend on the project tooling crate. Its A glyph has an
advance of 400 units per em. The browser and native text probes use the same bytes.
`cyrillic-400.ttf` maps four Cyrillic code points, comma and exclamation to that glyph and is generated
deterministically by `scripts/generate-view-cyrillic-font.py` for layout tests.
`advance-900.ttf` is the companion synthetic font from the same browser-fixture
generator, with a 900-unit advance and no Cyrillic glyphs.
`bold-900.ttf` and `italic-900.ttf` are synthetic alternate faces of
`Varta Fixture 400`, generated by the corresponding `scripts/generate-view-*-font.py` scripts.
`password.ttf` is generated by `scripts/generate-view-password-font.py`. Its
original small square mask differs visibly from the tall plaintext rectangles,
so native password tests can detect accidental plaintext painting.

`clusters.ttf` and `clusters-partial.ttf` are original synthetic faces generated
by `scripts/generate-view-cluster-font.py`. Their combining glyphs have zero
advance, while A advances 400 or 900 units respectively. U+035C expands through
`ccmp` into three glyphs; U+035D remains one. The partial face omits U+035C so
coverage after a long prefix can select the complete fallback. Tests count real
shaped glyphs and enforce the existing painting budget. Both files regenerate
byte-for-byte with fixed timestamps (verified with fontTools 4.60.2); fontTools is
needed only for regeneration.

`expansion.ttf` is the same original generator's 16-glyph-per-mark face. It
exercises intermediate shaping-array refusal before a large result enters the
layout and successful reuse after refusal. It also regenerates deterministically;
its glyph outlines/metrics are original, with no third-party font data.

`aat-current.ttf`, `aat-marked.ttf`, `aat-loop.ttf`, `aat-kern.ttf` and
`aat-kerx.ttf` are original derivatives of the cluster fixture, regenerated by
`scripts/generate-view-aat-fonts.py`. Their raw AAT tables encode finite current/
marked insertion, a nonadvancing loop, legacy kern and extended kerx state
machines. Fixed timestamps and original outlines make all five reproducible;
no platform font data is copied. Tests shape the fonts through the actual native
pipeline and sweep budgets below/exactly at the observed completed-work count.

`unicode.ttf` is generated by `scripts/generate-view-unicode-font.py` with fixed
timestamps and original bar/square/mark outlines. It covers the paragraph tests'
symbols, supplementary scalar, accented Latin, combining mark, Hebrew, Arabic,
CJK and nonbreaking space. Distinct glyphs expose visual run ordering; cmap
aliases allow exact native pixel comparisons and an independent Chrome canvas
check of that ordering. The synthetic glyphs test shaping and geometry, not
natural-script typography or complete font coverage. Regeneration requires
fontTools; no platform font is copied.

`inline.ttf` is generated by `scripts/generate-view-inline-font.py`. Original
outlines and fixed timestamps supply an AA ligature with a distinctive advance,
a combining mark and Arabic joining forms with distinctive outlines. Native and
Chrome probes use identical bytes to test shared shaping, cluster ownership and
inline font geometry. It is not a real-font typography acceptance fixture.
